Distribution. This species is known to occur only in the southern Mexican state of Oaxaca (Fig. 7). The localities where Limnocoris rodriguesi was collected are in the Sierra Madre del Sur biogeographic province; more specifically, in the westernmost district of Tierras Altas Oaxaqueñas. Rodrigues & Sites (2019) reported five specimens (2 ♂, 2 ♀ UMC; 1 ♀ MZUSP) of L. signoreti from San Mateo Yetla in norther Oaxaca. A closer examination of the specimens revealed that four of them belong to L. rodriguesi and only one male (UMC) belongs to L. signoreti. Limnocoris rodriguesi was collected syntopically with L. pygmaeus at Río Rana (L- 1906) and La Cuchara (L- 1396) and with L. signoreti at San Mateo Yetla (13 - X- 1990). Additionally, this species was collected syntopically with several species of Naucoridae in the genus Ambrysus, including: A. baeus Polhemus & Polhemus, A. henryi Reynoso & Sites, A. schuhi Reynoso & Sites, A. sitesi Reynoso, and A. spicatus La Rivers at Río Rana (L- 1906); and with A. pygmaeus La Rivers at La Cuchara (L- 1396), and with A. pygmaeus and A. spicatus at Putla de Guerrero (L- 1397). Furthermore, this species was also collected syntopically with the saucer bug and rock-clinging species Cataractocoris macrocephalus (Montandon) at the type locality. The state of Oaxaca is known for its high biodiversity, including that of insects. The stream at the type locality is the habitat of at least seven species of Naucoridae in three genera (Ambrysus, Cataractocoris Usinger, Limnocoris), including the three recently described species Ambrysus henryi, A. schuhi, and A. sitesi. Habitat description. The type locality at Río Rana (L- 1906), close to the town of San Miguel Mixtepec, is in the south-central area of the Mexican state of Oaxaca, at an elevation of 712 meters. The stream at this location is 5 – 10 meters wide, with fast current, and boulders, cobble, and gravel (Fig. 8).
